title: A Nagata ring is universally Japanese (Nagata)
statement: Let $R$ be a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]. Then $R$ is universally Japanese [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]: for every ring map $R\to S$ of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] with $S$ an integral domain, $S$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], i.e. for every finite extension $L$ of the fraction field of $S$ the integral closure of $S$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $S$-module.

proof.text: Use the zero-variable polynomial isomorphism to R for the base of induction. In the successor step use the isomorphism R[X_0,...,X_n] = (R[X_0,...,X_{n-1}])[X_n], apply the one-variable polynomial-Nagata lemma, and transport Nagata along that finite isomorphism using finiteness over Nagata.

For a finite type domain algebra S over R, choose a surjective R-algebra map from a polynomial ring in finitely many variables to S. The source is Nagata by induction. The surjective map is finite (its target is generated as a module by 1), so finiteness over Nagata makes S Nagata.
Apply the Nagata-domain N-2 lemma to S. Since S was any finite type domain algebra over R, this is precisely IsUniversallyJapanese R.
